Retryable decline recovers within bounded dunning policy
Definitive terminal decline stops according to the contract
Awaiting-method expiry and paid-access cutoff are exact
Unknown provider result remains distinct from declined or unpaid
A failing due pass makes one attempt and holds back no other merchant's renewal
Cancel then resume before cutoff preserves the paid runway
Cancellation concurrent with admitted renewal preserves custody
Terminal cancellation retains durable remote-delete obligation
Agreement revocation and late callback cannot revive future billing
Cancellation after boundary follows irreversible rail policy
Cancel, resume and cancel again inside the paid period never extends access past it

A Stripe resume Stripe cannot be told of (provider writes off) is refused, and nothing commits

Required customer action completes the accepted change once
Concurrent renewal and change retain one financial agreement

Scheduled price migration moves only eligible subscriptions at boundary
Failed push is retried by its operation without a duplicate migration or push
Cancellation leaves completed and ineligible subscriptions unchanged
Active financial lease preserves its original terms
Partial refund 1000 then final refund 2000 exactly returns a 3000-unit charge
Concurrent overlapping refunds cannot exceed refundable value
Response-loss refund converges from provider evidence once
Foreign merchant and unsupported refund are refused with original currency and account intact
A dashboard refund lands from the reversals read while the full provider read cannot finish, and once

Two partial CCBill refunds naming one sale are booked as two reversals, an exact replay of either books nothing, and a refund beyond what remains of the sale books nothing and raises a ledger finding naming it
A won dispute gives back what its chargeback took: the charge reads refunded only by its net reversals, in its detail and in the merchant's list
External payment records exact known amount without outgoing charge
Same provider transaction replay creates no duplicate payment or credit
Conflicting merchant customer or account linkage is refused
Imported settled payment retains original refund allowance and event identity
Grant 1000 reserve 600 capture 450 release 150 leaves 550 available units

Credit ledger and financial event roll back together
Batch admit capture release and extend report accurate per-item results
Concurrent terminal actions resolve one reservation once
Same request ID with changed payload is refused
Local Tx commit persists host and admission outcome together
Local Tx rollback leaves no reservation charge or event
A resent usage item answers its receipt and a changed one conflicts
Late usage and a changed meter keep the accepted pricing
A refused item leaves its neighbours and another merchant's lease
Known usage group and pagination returns exact seeded totals
Charged failed usage resent past its key window is charged once
A lost reply's resend settles once and a gap is refused
A dead lease's outbox resend with close settles each item once and releases its request hold
A batch job's lost first reply posts its usage once
A thousand items are priced exactly on their total
Pricing periods are priced apart; a lease's request hold captures at its pinned cards and other usage at the cards in force
A month's usage posts once and once more before a top-up, held until then
Views of an occasional customer on ten leases reserve nothing, count every live lease, and show what settled
A sync with close settles its usage, releases the lease's request holds and clears its report; a closed lease owns no new hold and its usage still settles
A lapsed lease's in-flight report and request holds count nowhere until it syncs again
Lease ids are UUIDv7: another version is invalid_param, an id older than the replay horizon with no lease is lease_not_found, and a usage-only close ends an earlier lease, which then owns no hold
A view's pricing follows the cards in force, and gate usage settles at the cards in force when it settles
What a day's usage leaves owed is dated on its day, so the bill of the period that holds it bills it whenever it posted
Usage after a credit lot lapses never draws it: the lot pays for the usage before its lapse and expires with the rest
A lease keeps each refused item's number and code within a byte bound: a resend answers them and the lease keeps syncing
Views answer per customer and currency and limit sets per invoker attributes; a host-stated set claims only money
A trust level's policy is its own limit set, and usage reported with its attributes counts in its spend window
A view never opens a session; the first settled use opens it at its admission, and usage admitted in it counts there after it ends
admit_while_positive: the server admits the request that crosses the limit once and refuses the next
No hold holds past the 30-day hold lifetime, an abandoned admission in a long window included
Concurrent syncs (usage, reports, views) and lease admissions on the same customers never deadlock and settle every report once
A sync that cannot take its locks within its lock budget is answered 503 service_unavailable before the commit guard, commits and renews nothing, and its retry settles once
Trust levels whose spend windows share a key but not a cap carry their own capacities and are each refused by their own cap

Usage without a grant opens no window of any reset kind, so a late buyer gets the whole capacity and unpaid use starts no session; usage while a grant has lapsed is not enforced but counts in the windows the grant opened while they last, which the returning grant reads

A sync settles a bounded prefix of its usage, the items of at most 100 customers within a time budget, and leaves the rest neither settled nor refused, so a backlog across a thousand customers drains over several syncs and settles each item once

A meter correction fences only its own merchant's usage of the meter's event types: it takes no table lock, its own merchant's settlement waits for its transaction, and another merchant's usage settles while it is open
A batch reporter's usage-only sync (lease id and numbered usage) answers through_n, refused and receipts as before
Usage counts in the spend windows of the invoker attributes it reports, batch usage with none in the customer's own

Without ClickHouse usage, admissions, limits, usage catalog declarations, usage settings and usage metrics answer event_store_required in process and over HTTP, a gate refuses for good, and subscriptions, credit packs, running charges and usage orders work
New applies the ClickHouse migrations once however often it starts, a checking start refuses an unmigrated store, and a store with another identity than the one the database recorded is refused
GET /v1/config reports usage true with ClickHouse and false without
A view request no admission would take, or whose customer's policy cannot be resolved, is refused alone: the sync settles its usage (in no spend window for that customer) and answers its other views
Usage counts in the spend window current at its admission to the millisecond: items admitted either side of a window's end in one second count apart
A request hold a lapsed lease makes counts at once for every other admission, and stops when the lease never syncs again
A sync whose in-flight report first names a customer another transaction holds the spend lock of commits without waiting for it
The view of a sync that captures a lease's request hold settles what the capture moved past the hold's estimate
A resend after a sync whose events reached the store but whose transaction never committed inserts nothing twice: raw usage, FINAL and the rollups agree
While ClickHouse is out of reach a sync answers 503 and settles nothing, a usage customer's balance and top-up wait for it, a customer without usage is unaffected, and every item settles once after
A period posts the price of its total: graduated across two postings, a volume crossing carried and credited once its late window closed, a card revision priced card by card
Late usage of a month that posted posts the difference at the next close
Fixed, session, rolling, rate, billing-period and lifetime limits read their use from the event store, and an item admitted before a reset counts in the window it was admitted in
New refuses a database with unposted usage without its store and an empty store; usage attach discards the unposted usage only with --discard-unposted, on the record
A SCIM user erasure clears its usage events' invoker and metadata and its history's invokers, and keeps quantities and money
A billing archive carries the merchant's usage; restore refuses without an event store or into a merchant with usage there, and restores it into an empty one
Equal lease ids and numbers under two merchants are two events, each counted by its merchant
A month's usage posts at the month's end in the merchant's accounting zone, not UTC's
Usage history folds into the days of the merchant's accounting zone (23:30 in Kolkata is that day), a zone change regroups the past, and the days sum to what posts
A capture retried after a commit that was lost, and a lease item that names no occurred_at resent after one, each find the event the first attempt inserted and charge once
An item resent after a commit that was lost counts in the session window its first attempt opened, not one opened at the resend
A sync whose caller gives up while its insert is sent still finishes the insert before it lets go of its locks: the resend inserts nothing and the rollups count each item once
A lot lapsing mid-month funds exactly the usage and running charges before its lapse, however much usage came after it; only that usage is owed
Usage the event store lost after it posted is not a price that fell: usage since is charged on top of what posted, and nothing that posted is credited back
A usage erasure that stopped between folding the history and deleting its invokers' rows, run again, leaves each event in the history once
Usage priced under a card print whose intake never committed holds up no posting: a print a card in force names is recorded again, and one nothing names is left out
Start and stop charge account for the exact known elapsed segment
Concurrent or repeated stop never bills a segment twice
Crash around final segment preserves durable stop outcome
Insufficient funds refuse admission; depletion signals host stop without resurrection
Opted-in date or threshold creates and collects one usage obligation
Subscription-only host starts no usage billing sweep
Paid waived and uncollectible debt is not charged again
Delinquency clears correctly after payment or approved debt action
Purchase and grant overlap yields correct union of entitlement windows
Revoke or expire one source preserves another valid source
Exact start end and historical tenure boundaries agree
Refunded or archived content follows declared access and retained-history policy
Subscription boundary repair records grant termination and never restores forbidden future access
Subscription closure is atomic under rollback and concurrent replay and leaves other sources intact
Missing projection repair rechecks a chargeback recorded after detection
Ordinary cancellation and uncertain subscription state preserve purchased grants
An ended subscription window still applies its recorded grant revocation without repeated repair
Valid signed callback binds correct PSP account and environment
Tampered missing or wrong-account signature is refused
Secret rotation accepts overlap and rejects it after deadline
Duplicate and out-of-order callback settles once without regression
Callback during active fetch causes a durable follow-up observation
A thin Stripe event is read back from Stripe at its object's canonical URL and settles once, like its snapshot
Another merchant's claim of a PSP or custodian account in the other money class is refused by file, and the owner's webhooks keep working
One merchant's live and test PSPs on one account each receive the events their own secret verifies; Stripe's livemode attributes one both verify; one neither verifies is refused
Crash before provider submission resumes one authorized operation
Checkout process death after provider acceptance repairs order/payment outcome from stored evidence
Expired lease with two workers retains one execution authority
Catalog edit deployment skew or supersession cannot erase unresolved money
GC retention and archive refuse to discard unresolved financial evidence

Wrong tenant occupied target or corrupt archive fails atomically
Copied book blocks provider writes until explicitly authorized
Unresolved operation refuses export without changing custody or source write posture
NMI receipts that name their card export and restore verbatim
An archive written before the unread tables and columns were dropped still restores
An archive written before the custody migration record was dropped still restores
A Solana pull scheduled ahead and restored with its merchant runs on the destination at its due time
A merchant's notification adoption export holds back no other merchant and its own producers commit after its snapshot

Credit lots move out of grants with their ids and the remainders and pending-refund shares the old formulas gave (the reservation net of reversals already settled), old data the move cannot place refuses it with nothing moved, and a migrated purchase deposit replays

Stored limit rate cards migrate to counts: a per-unit card becomes one count and a matrix one per priced cell with its filter, the limit's field owner renames, and a card counts cannot express refuses the migration with nothing changed
A paid Stripe hosted-page order exports and restores with its attempt's Checkout Session state
A database whose months differ from a fresh build and whose baseline record carries other content is accepted and re-stamped by the migration step with its rows intact
A start that skips migrations is refused on a baseline record of other content until the migration step has run
Open limit windows and staff adjustments move with the book: lifetime and current-window usage and adjustments survive a round trip
Provision find list and rename merchant retain stable identity
Concurrent or too-early rename respects ownership and cooldown
Delete or retire refuses active obligations and closes authority
Unused merchant retirement releases exact group and retries preserve a reclaimed name owner
Operator CLI purge confirms its inventory and the job queued with it deletes the merchant's Vault configuration
Merchant purge removes the directory's contacts and provisioning tokens
A merchant purge whose deletion from the event store fails commits and queues the job that deletes it, which River retries until the store takes it
Destructive ceiling records and enforces hold for original actor and command
Wrong authority cannot clear a hold or evade it through impersonation
Reviewed clear resumes held action without replaying prior financial effects
Finding resolution cannot bypass destructive incident authority
Targeted verification recovers a missed flag and holds a provider-confirmed cancel until the switch allows it
Held webhook cancel parks the subscription with access and converges once the switch allows it
One-off transfer binds treasury and mint and rejects underpayment
Recurring pull persists signed operation before submission and resumes safely
Unknown transaction waits while confirmed or reverted evidence resolves correctly
Duplicate confirmations and workers cannot debit one period twice
Wrong instruction authority account stale blockhash or insufficient gas is refused safely
Retried recurring pull keeps its backoff and then renews the period once
A pull signed with a low cranker wallet raises a finding that the next funded pull resolves
Merchant customer reads retain billing state without hosted account-link storage

An application without the provisioning permission neither reads nor writes the directory
Contact erasures keep a budget and holds of their own, and an erasure past it waits rather than fails
A waiting erasure takes the contact at once and a report older than it cannot restore it
Existing customer proof is read-only and never enrolls or requires recent sign-in
Customer proof preserves credential, issuer, merchant and tenant boundaries
Asserted and sender-constrained resource proofs preserve their original authority
Customer proof refuses expiry, revocation and unavailable authority after storage waits
Host customer admission policy preserves original proof and fixed billing scope ceilings
Personal access token reads as its customer and holds its permissions but never pays or takes a person-only action
Merchant tenant binding adopts with its group in one transaction, replays as a no-op, refuses another tenant and never changes
A customer route refuses a signed-in account of another tenant than its merchant's binding
Every catalog route refuses a bound credential without its permission and admits its root twin

Merchant and hosted vault custody retain original card and charge authority through recovery and removal

Host workers on a composed fleet keep River's job timeout and crash rescue

Limit reads and adjustments stay within their merchant, customer and permission
A customer reads its own limits at /v1/me/limits
A five-hour session and a weekly cap in weighted tokens: first use opens the session, a hold keeps its window, the crossing request finishes and the next is refused limit_reached
Balance and a monthly spend cap: one request holds and settles both or neither
Four replicas racing for a limit's last units admit exactly its capacity
An overrun settles past capacity unclamped, refuses holds until a refill, and records reached_at once
A delegated invoker is refused as before and holds no money and no limit
Invokers with the same limits share their windows; another trust level is held against its own
Remote and embedded gates decide with the same code; a warm decision needs no I/O and a view keeps deciding while OpenRails is unreachable
Racing requests on two limits never take more than either limit; eighty taken of a hundred and thirty captured leaves seventy
A lost sync reply and a restart with unsent usage converge once, with and without an outbox; a stopped lease holds nothing
A gate ticket lives across many syncs without a deadline and its capture settles in the session it was admitted in
Gate refusals are verdicts (limit_reached with its reset); near the limit the server decides as a request hold of the lease; OpenRails down is ErrUnavailable for a cold customer
A gate's in-flight report counts as held for admissions (Admit and AdmitTx, limits and balance) while its lease lives; an empty report clears it
Closing a gate settles its usage, releases its request holds and clears its in-flight report before its lease would lapse
A spend window that names no currency is in its policy's policy_currency, converted to the request's
A billing policy's amounts are in its policy_currency: an accrual-rate cap in yen gates USD usage at its converted rate

A limit counting two meters by weight (output four times input, a large model's output six more) admits and refuses at the weighted total in Admit and in a gate, and settles each count rounded half up
A catalog naming a limit's rate_cards is refused with their rename to counts, as YAML and over HTTP, and applies nothing; the one-to-one count applies
Four gates racing a small balance with steady traffic overshoot at most one request each, and every admitted request settles once
Two gates and an unreachable OpenRails keep deciding on their views and together spend at most what was left, each its share
Near zero every request is decided on the server, one at a time: two gates racing for the last unit admit exactly one
An idle gate stops syncing and its lease lapses out of the gate count; its stale view decides one request and the next waits for a sync
A fixed window that resets between syncs is decided from the view's next window with no sync, and settles there
One merchant's failed background pass fails its job after the other merchants finish
A Solana renewal whose scheduled pull is still owed is not a missed rebill
Declared CCBill charge is recorded by the pull that reads it, otherwise kept as a finding without a payment
PSP import and its queued job commit together
A PSP's environment proof expires after an hour and is proven again before the next write; an account that changed environment is refused
A live Stripe key of the declared account passes the production write gate; one of another account is Mismatched and writes nothing
Expired vault card is updated at its Account Updater, as a new token or a new expiry, and its renewal retries on it
Vault card with no update after an expired decline asks the customer once
Ahead-of-renewal refresh asks armed vaults about due cards only, including cards awaiting a method, and retries a throttled vault without marking cards checked
PSP-held card declined as expired asks the customer with no refresh
An unmapped NMI plan blocks its subscriptions until a person maps it from the observed catalog; re-apply lands once
A Stripe price the provider deactivated is retired: not a tier-change target, still billing
A plan-less CCBill member lands only on the one PSP price its rebill equals or a person's pick
The pull observes the whole provider catalog read-only, deleted and inline objects included
The Stripe catalog read keeps the newest observation, retires prices of archived or deleted products and skips what it cannot read
Loading PSPs, in one process or another, pulls none; a person pulls each NMI, Stripe and CCBill PSP, history from the earliest object, landing nothing; Solana has no import
A provider refusing a PSP's credentials fails the import with psp_credentials_rejected; neither a reload nor replaced credentials restart it; a person's new pull reads them
A provider that does not answer is retried past five attempts with a capped backoff; the import stays pulling and resumes without reading the roster again
Applying an onboarding import lands each rail's subscriptions, payments and NMI vault once; re-apply and a later manual import duplicate nothing
A landed Stripe customer attributes a later out-of-band subscription; a customer mapping another keeps it; one another customer holds is a conflict for only its customer
A PSP added to a running process is not pulled; a refused pull stays failed when its credentials rotate, and a person's new pull reads the rotated ones
A provider answer no attempt can read fails the import after five attempts with its error, deletable

An NMI import lands each schedule in its mapped price's currency, NMI's decimal read exactly (1000.00 as 1000 JPY, 12.50 as 12.50 EUR); an amount not exact in that currency or a plan with no price stays blocked; a book's schedule in another currency than its price's is refused

A person pulls a PSP from the console, which shows the pull's phases to pulled; one record is linked by hand, the unmapped plan mapped as an archived price, and two applies land each subscription once, no provider write; the price page's Verify reads the provider price's verification
A 150-row mappings CSV goes out in two requests and deletes one mapping; re-link links by rule; a CCBill subscription two prices match lands on the price a person picks

After a reconcile and Apply the console groups the open proposal; approving the access-ending change is held, dismissing needs notes, a stale approval answers already resolved; a pull finding offers Review, not Resolve
An unmapped price's finding routes to provider prices; mapping a parked Stripe signup's price from the Parked page lands it once and resolves the finding
A refused pull shows its credentials error and settings link with no records; a configuration reader sees every console page with no action and writes nothing; Map needs catalog manage
A Stripe price event that first shows a live unmapped price raises one medium finding; redeliveries and bursts add nothing, retiring resolves it, pulled prices raise none
A Stripe signup on an unmapped price parks without retries and lands exactly once, with its bill, when the price is mapped
A Stripe subscription whose customer is linked to no one parks with a high finding and lands once when the customer is linked
A held Stripe subscription moved onto an unmapped price keeps its paid tier and parks; mapping the price moves it once
A mapping committed while converge reads the unmapped price strands no park: the park re-reads it under its lock
An NMI subscription OpenRails does not hold is adopted for the vault's one owner on a mapped plan, parks otherwise, waits for the first pull and drops order ids
A parked subscription an import lands closes as landed and its finding resolves
Two hosts on one merchant and schema park once and land one subscription and one payment
Parked subscriptions list newest first by PSP, reason and release, paged, for merchant configuration readers only
With no import yet, an unlinked Stripe subscription parks with its high finding, and linking its customer lands it at once and resolves the finding
A held Stripe subscription ends only when Stripe answers resource_missing; any other 404 fails its converge, which retries with access intact
A held NMI subscription ends only when NMI answers E_NOT_FOUND; E_ROUTE_NOT_FOUND fails its converge, which retries with access intact
An NMI schedule OpenRails does not hold that names no plan raises a high finding naming it once no import stages it, parks nothing, and the finding resolves when NMI deletes it

Only an import that is pulling, or stages a subscription unlanded, owns it: before any import and after a failed one its park raises a finding, a pulling import resolves it, and that pull failing wakes the park to raise it again
A manual reconcile stages what OpenRails does not hold, proposes every difference in what it holds and lands nothing until a person applies
A pull after a host's legacy book corrects price, schedule and start; ending access waits for a person
A host's legacy book after a pull skips provider rows; a webhook converge hands a host row to the provider
A host row landed after the pull is held and corrected at Apply, never landed twice
A row that moved after the roster read gets no state proposal and says so; its money facts are still proposed
A paid Stripe move to another product's price is proposed and waits for a person; an unpaid one proposes nothing
An NMI roster implausibly small against the live book fails the import and raises nothing
Only a person or the in-process host approves, dismisses or applies; approve is idempotent per key; one import per PSP in flight; a superseded import is not linked or applied
A dismissed correction stays dismissed while the provider only moves its period, and an Apply never approves it
An operator refresh between a pull and its Apply leaves the pull's proposals untouched
Proposal cancellations spend the actor allowance per affected subscription and a replay spends nothing
Upgrade retires scheduled provider refreshes and the operator command coalesces requests and retries the same job
A failed PSP import cannot be applied
A price picked for an import record is never deleted

A correction adopts an ended row's cancel kind and date from the provider at Apply, never into or out of a chargeback and never for an unpaid Stripe subscription; status, period and access stay byte-identical and the provider sees no write
Numeric CCBill references survive host import replay and archive validation while real cards are refused
CCBill webhooks naming a 19-digit id apply to the legacy row stored without its leading zero, which takes the provider's spelling; another number matches nothing
A CCBill DataLink import holds and respells a legacy row stored without the leading zero, and links through a zero-dropped legacy mapping
A CCBill provider refresh respells a zero-dropped legacy row to the roster's id and records its rebill

A CCBill pull that may not write the mirror, advisory or enforce without inserts, matches a zero-dropped legacy row by identity against a complete roster: nothing reads as missing, gone or canceled, and the row keeps its spelling

A CCBill sale that arrives after its lapsed page's order was paid by card is recorded once against the order as a payment held for refund, with a late-payment finding to refund it at CCBill and a repair to cancel its CCBill subscription; it grants nothing, the card keeps paying the order, the card is never refunded, and a replay changes nothing

The dashboard keeps every stat label within two lines at any column width, legends a one-rail donut and names PSPs by key; staff lists name the customer and plan, and still list by id with the directory down; customer controls find a customer by name and offer its currencies; a membership with no other plan offers Change subscription disabled, saying why; ending a membership from the console says the customer loses access now once End access now is ticked; an ended membership offers no plan or card change; clearing a hold confirms it and drops it from Ops; at 1440 the findings table shows Resolve unscrolled; a missing customer, subscription or payment is reported once, by its page
A subscription end the provider confirmed is stored as the provider's: read back, a later renewal is kept for refund review and does not reopen it
A CCBill cancel the pull lands is a lapse, and the member's reactivation and rebill restore access
A CCBill Cancellation is a lapse: a reactivation inside the paid period resumes it, and a late rebill past it restores it
A failed-rebill cancel on a provider's or a chargeback's end tightens it and keeps its kind: a later rebill does not reopen it
Lapsed credit stops being available at its lapse and its balance watch, arrears included, expires it
Retention cleanup alone ages out unpaid orders, stale gate leases and orphan state; order expiry alone expires abandoned attempts
A migration move that no longer applies is skipped, terminally, and its migration settles
A migration needs notice when what the customer pays per unit of time rises, at the seats its renewal bills; a one-time target is refused
Kill switch turned off during a provider pull holds that pull's convergence retractions
Only an in-process handle acts for a named person; a remote handle refuses ActingFor
A reservation that never starts, left by a crash or refused at its start, stops holding budget
A reservation started past its life is admitted against the budget again
With the destructive switch off a spent Solana schedule waits past due with access
A billing import, by the host or staff, cancels only through the destructive switch, the PSP cancellation cap and an admission on the merchant's budget recording its actor
A staff card removal is a staff admission and spends no customer-action budget
A declined charge that spends dunning in a billing import is an admitted cancel, held while the switch is off
A lost admission answer leaves no action spending the budget
A merchant's books land one at a time
An abandon waiting on its actions stalls no other admission
A provider-seen NMI decline opens dunning and schedules its retry in one transaction
Held awaiting-method expiry leaves the due pass until its recheck
Due pass queues an NMI retry and never waits on the gateway
A lost card's renewal refuses a same-card customer payment with no provider call and admits another card
An NMI decline whose issuer code forbids a reattempt waits for a new card, and retry-now on that card is refused with no provider call
Network do-not-retry advice on a generic decline stops dunning on the card
A decline the cardholder can clear is retried by the customer on the same card up to the cap
A softly declined monthly renewal is retried on days 3, 5, 7 and 10 and canceled at its fifth failure
A merchant's customer retry cap is honoured at none, the default and a raised value, and another card is always admitted
A dunning policy whose retries could pass the card networks' reattempt limits is refused
A dunning policy that omits the transient ladder keeps the built-in one, and an empty list has none
Rebill watch backs off a failing provider probe
Admission refuses under the customer's own delinquency policy
Marked cards never starve a planned ahead-of-renewal check
Mastercard 51 through 55 uses 16 digits; other supported cards and formatted values remain blocked
Each Stripe account charges and saves cards on its own customer; another account's customer is never reused or overwritten
A card number in any field of a card save or order payment but the typed card is refused before a provider sees it
A HyperSwitch card save consults the card-testing ledger: a blocked customer never reaches HyperSwitch

Legitimate phone numbers, UUIDs, Solana addresses and numeric order ids pass the firewall on every card route, which refuses a card number; a card number as a field name is not echoed and no test header is stored
A declared or changed Stripe PSP registers its webhook endpoint at once
A Dashboard-registered endpoint of a file-declared Stripe PSP is managed, not refused
Job health reads overrunning, discarded and completed jobs from River; the progress probe fails without a leader or on an overrunning job
With no rescue window set, River rescues crashed OpenRails and host jobs after ten minutes, and a long pass only past its timeout
The usage pass bills past a full page of due accounts in a continuation job
Retention cleanup continues past a full batch of merchants in a new job and reaches every merchant
Partition retention drops a month of holds and the month of their parts in one pass once it is past the replay horizon, and keeps the current month
Paying, waiving or writing off a usage order clears its customer's delinquency in the same change
An overdue usage order is told once without automatic usage billing
A usage account billed in full is not due again until it spends
The usage pass queues a due collection as an operation its own job charges
Admission refuses credit that lapsed before its balance watch expired it
A running charge is billed through the bill date before any daily posting runs
A direct NMI collection refused before dispatch retains nonexecution proof and recovers without duplicate payment
Usage of a billed day reported after its usage order is owed after that order's period and billed by the next order
Usage before a period that ends within a day is owed in that period, not the next one
Revoking the collection agreement posts today's usage on the revocation's clock and bills it in the final usage order
A declined usage-order collection retries on the merchant's dunning_policy, not the built-in schedule
A billing policy's delinquency floor is in its policy_currency and holds only debt in it; other debt meets its own currency's floor

A billing policy's outstanding cap and collection threshold bind only money in its policy_currency: a yen policy neither refuses dollar admission nor withholds dollar collection, which follows the dollar collection_threshold
A usage order whose total is not a whole cent is paid by card, and its change is a credit lot bought at face
A due Solana pull runs as the operation its period scheduled, a margin after the period end
A pull the chain refuses before its period end is retried, not taken as already paid
A dropped Solana pull is signed again only once it provably never landed, and a landed pull is never repeated
A wallet that is the plan's cranker is refused a co-signed subscribe; the cranker signs nothing for it
A Solana upgrade the wallet lands and never confirms is recorded from the chain: one charge, no revocation, the new plan pulled at renewal
A Solana downgrade the wallet lands and never confirms is recorded from the chain and renews on the lower plan
A prepared Solana plan change whose transaction provably never landed is released
A Solana plan change's confirm and the chain read record one change, in either order
A pull the old Solana subscription refuses while its plan change is pending cancels nothing
An import queues, with its own commit, the one read of the charges it attributed
An imported purchase line whose list total leaves int64 is refused without a payment
A boot reconciles a Stripe webhook endpoint only when its configuration changed
A superseded Stripe webhook endpoint is retired by the pass scheduled at its deadline
An unresolved undeclared account alerts its operator again once a day
A Stripe PSP changed while its pass runs reaches Stripe without waiting for the backstop
A finding alert whose first delivery fails is delivered by its job's retry, once
A PSP whose webhooks went silent while pulls find its charges raises a finding; one with no charges or no webhooks does not, and it clears when webhooks resume
A refund the ledger cannot book alerts the operator once
A low Solana cranker alerts the operator once
A refused message sender alerts the operator once
A rate-limited customer alerts the operator once
A held terminal outcome alerts the operator once
Distinct repairs of one transaction alert separately
An engine renewal nothing attempted by its deadline reads as missed without a recorded miss
A provider-billed grace that ends unanswered is read by id from the due pass
An overdue provider-billed renewal is asked by id from the due pass before the rebill watch reads NMI
A provider-declared failure inside the merchant's longer dunning schedule stays in dunning: converge reads the subscription's case policy, not the built-in window
A provider-declared failure is judged by its own cycle's window: past a weekly schedule's, it is not dunned however long the monthly window is
An NMI renewal the probe cannot settle is read by id once its grace passes
A complete provider refresh queues no due work: the hourly billing pass takes it
A roster page NMI cuts short resolves no unverified row; the next whole read does
A grant commits with its customer convergence job or not at all
A revoked last window tells the customer through the revoke convergence
A timed window that lapses is told once by the hourly health pass
A provider operation that ended without an explicit decline stays an abandoned-operation finding; only a decline raises none and closes an open one
The hourly health pass raises held engine renewals and closes them once attempted
An NMI history read that fails fails the billing pass; the next pass reads it
Imported admin grant windows change at the evidence horizon and replay without extra history
Imported admin grant refusals preserve other book rows and host declarations restore staff-revoked access
Concurrent imported grant declarations and lost responses replay once
The merchant SDK reuses scoped allowed entitlement keys, never denials, through their scheduled cutoff
A purchase after a cached entitlement check is visible on the next check
A product-access grant requires an Idempotency-Key and a retry under it grants once
Exact checks and prefix pages stay on their indexes for a customer holding 10,000 of 40,000 products
An engine renewal is billed by the next hourly billing pass; its renewal grace reaches two passes past the due instant, so access holds across the gap
An NMI period its schedule skipped is collected and retried by the hourly billing passes the day it is found, with access kept
A credit lot lapsing at 00:00 UTC is never spent past it and is booked by that hour's billing pass
A delinquency grace end is evaluated by the next hourly billing pass, the same day
An order past its expiry is refused payment at once and tidied by the next hourly billing pass
A billing pass that fails partway runs its other scans, and the pass after a missed hour takes everything still due
Job progress fails once a billing pass records critical work a day overdue and clears after a clean pass
A live provider operation whose River wake was lost is queued again by the first billing pass an hour past its due time
A hold, a revocation or a lapse that takes a balance to its line commits the balance's look and its notice lands within seconds
A hold or a capture that leaves a balance above its line queues no look
A balance look that fails leaves its watch due and the next billing pass delivers its notice
A transfer landing after its order's expiry, before any expiry pass, is held for review as session_closed
A challenge or hosted-page confirm past the order's expiry closes it before any pass; money that moved after expiry settles the order it closed
An open order past its expiry claims nothing: preview, merchant and cart orders buy its lines before any pass
An open order past its expiry reads expired, without next action or payment options, in every read and list, and cannot be canceled
A card save confirmed or saved again past its 24-hour cutoff, before any pass, is removed
NMI card erasure completes only after provider confirmation
A card with permanent versions is never hard-deleted
A card an unverified membership bills cannot be removed
An order expiry backlog past one batch is expired by one billing pass
A billing pass that starts while another still runs exits without running a scan; the running pass takes what is due
An engine boots on a borrowed pool built from settings, with no connection string, and refuses one without a pool
A Vault KV mount with no Vault client is refused and reported, and merchant configuration answers unavailable
A slug declared twice provisions neither entry and is reported; the other declarations serve

The generated client gets the server's own refusals: a malformed query value is invalid_query before any handler, a batch or field the client no longer checks is the server's invalid_param, and an empty path segment is refused before any I/O
Every logger the engine and the standalone server reach is set, the default logger is untouched, and a refusal is logged with its route, request and merchant
A Vault merchant document naming a retired key is refused with what replaced it, as a manifest is
A billing pass that waited behind a balance's look leaves the watch that look moved on
A customer's running charges count toward its accrual_rate_cap at their rates while they run
While ClickHouse is out of reach a balance look at a customer without unposted usage expires its lapsed lot
A provider operation scheduled ahead is no stuck finding however long ago it was queued; one a day past its attempt, or parked or failing for a day, is
A Stripe downgrade schedules the new price for the subscription's seats
An upgrade in the microsecond its membership started ends the superseded period after it starts
A Stripe migration push keeps the subscription's seats, and a retry after a lost schedule create replays it
A published FX rate far from the one held is refused: once the held rate is stale, a euro price gets no Solana quote
A pending refund of a mixed order's credit line holds the line's whole credit lot until it settles
Refunds and chargebacks of a mixed order reverse the credit line first, then the rest, and a won dispute restores what it took
Credit a won dispute restores goes at once to an earlier refund that found the mixed order's credit line already returned
A credit lot's view equals its ledger counters after spend, expiry, revocation, refund and restore, and the ledger audit names a lot whose counters drift
A refunded credit pack's lot reads refunded and raises no refunded-source grant finding
Two credit lots that lapsed before their expiry ran expire only what each still holds after the usage settled at the first lapse
Every account type has one book and class; the general ledger refuses a merchant unit
A transfer across books, across currencies or naming another customer's account is refused
ledger-audit catches injected counter and rollup corruption
A credit lot whose deposit did not post is not spendable until convergence posts it once
A ledger from before the books migrates with rollups that ledger-audit and an export accept
Concurrent top-ups, one posting unposted usage first, all commit
An archive written before the books restores as the units book
A ledger transfer and an MRR change in either statement order, in two transactions held at commit, both commit
Two first checkouts in a currency a catalog apply opened overlap; a posting nothing opened for raises a finding; two checkouts and a usage collection in opposite lock orders all commit
An event queued before or after a ledger transfer, in two transactions held at commit, both commit
One transaction posting for two merchants in either order, two held at commit, both commit

A Stripe charge's fee and a dispute fee post once, exactly; a fee read again posts nothing new; a won dispute's and a refund's returned fees post back; a read that keeps failing waits for its finding and is read again once it is fixed; and a fee settled in another currency than the charge posts in that currency
A dispute's prevention refund is read through its dispute, never as a refund, even when it is booked after the dispute was read; the dispute's later change still posts its fees

New, expansion, contraction, churn and reactivation are each recorded once at the customer level, normalised to a month (calendar and named cadences divided by their months, a week 52/12, other windows 730.485 hours) and per currency
A cancellation at period end is scheduled churn with MRR unchanged; a resume reverses it; its end churns, dated at the end
A scheduled downgrade is scheduled contraction applied at its renewal; canceling the change reverses it
A Stripe cancel at period end mirrored from the portal is scheduled churn; a portal resume reverses it
A CCBill upgrade replacing its subscription nets to one expansion; an imported subscription opens MRR rather than counting as new

MRR at a past local day's start, across a daylight-saving change, read from 15-minute buckets equals its movements; with sequential scans off each report read, the scheduled ones included, and the due read still plan on an index
An engine upgrade replacing its subscription in one transaction nets to one expansion caused upgrade, with both subscriptions as its lines
A prune is a correction, not churn, and supersedes the pruned subscription's scheduled churn; undoing it is a correction back that schedules the churn again
A bulk import of thousands of subscriptions in one transaction settles once: reads of subscription_mrr grow with the book, not its square
The migration's backfill adopts a book written before MRR as backfilled openings in one settlement, its reads growing with the book

A declined renewal puts the subscription's MRR at risk as past due, listed and in mrr_at_risk; a paid retry closes the case recovered; dunning exhausted on a later renewal closes the next case churned, involuntary; the recovery rate is a half
A non-retryable decline puts MRR at risk as needing a payment method; a new card moves the same case to past due, and the paid retry recovers it
A card that expires before the renewal it pays for enters at risk on the period change that passes its expiry and leaves when the account updater refreshes it
A provider subscription OpenRails could not confirm is at risk while unverified and recovered when a read verifies its renewal
Usage delinquency puts the customer's subscription MRR in the currency at risk with the overdue amount beside it; paying the debt recovers it
The risk drain holds a customer's subscriptions while an NMI decline for the same customer queues it and waits: both commit, and the decline, queued after the claim, is re-evaluated by the next drain
A subscription at risk canceled at period end keeps its case open while it adds MRR; a resume continues the same case; canceled again, the end closes it churned, voluntary, once, at the end

A new default card that expires before the renewal puts the subscription following the default at risk through the queued change; an NMI schedule naming no card of its own is never at risk on the default
An upgrade of a subscription at risk closes its case superseded, counted in no recovery rate, and its replacement opens its own case
A merchant archive carries an open risk case, its episodes and at-risk MRR; the restore queues every customer with MRR, whom the target's drain re-evaluates

A customer whose risk evaluation fails alone is set aside with an mrr.risk.evaluation_failed finding while the rest of the merchant drains; set aside, it is skipped; a later evaluation takes its changes and closes the finding
A subscription at risk for its card, canceled at period end, still reads its card: a new expiry clears card_expiring and the case closes recovered
An NMI delivery signed under any nonce is accepted, with no replay window; a replay or retry of its event applies nothing
An NMI window read reaches a sale settled, refunded or voided after it: prune keeps its receipt, and still finds a receipt NMI does not list
A CCBill provider refresh reads DataLink in exports of at most 24 hours, which CCBill requires, and records every rebill of its eight-day windows

A live CCBill PSP refreshes in a job of its own, one DataLink request an hour: a day of transactions each, then the roster; a request CCBill refuses within the hour waits, and every rebill is recorded
A live CCBill PSP import reads its roster, then a day of history an hour, waiting between requests and resuming where it stopped until it is pulled
A CCBill cancellation whose webhook was missed, read from a paced day of transactions with no roster, cancels at the period end and keeps the time paid for
A CCBill account another merchant's current PSP holds in the same money class, in any subaccount, is refused as psp_exists before its credentials are probed
A signed NMI transaction event dated before its event_id record would be kept is acknowledged, applies nothing and raises life.webhook.replay_refused; one of its own time applies
An NMI chargeback batch is booked whatever its sales' dates: a chargeback of a sale 120 days old reverses it and cancels its membership, refused as no replay
A CCBill status read answering 1 for an unverified row whose paid period lapsed cancels it and keeps access through CCBill's expiration date
A CCBill rebill and the member's cancellation read in one export book the rebill, cancel, and keep access through the rebilled period's end

An NMI refresh backlog is read a link a run by last change, each ending at its end and advancing the applied watermark, the last through now; a sale settled in it is read in the link of its last change and booked once
A CCBill account another merchant archived, or holds only in the other money class, is declarable: only a current PSP of an unretired merchant in the same class holds it
A CCBill DataLink login CCBill refuses is psp_credentials_rejected and declares nothing; the probe is a subscription-management status read, which takes no DataLink hour

Two refused CCBill credential probes hold that login (account and username) an hour, across merchants and money classes: a third is psp_probe_limited with Retry-After and reaches no CCBill, and the account's owner on its own login is not held
A staff member grants a full batch of credit at once, one batch a minute; the merchant's own application is not metered
A paid one-off order sends one receipt: a replayed settlement queues no second message and a refused send is retried once
A fact written inside a billing restore queues no customer message; the same fact outside one queues one
A customer without an address is logged no_contact and the fact is still emitted
A fact on a test PSP is logged test_environment, sends nothing and is still emitted
Past ten messages an hour a customer's message is rate_limited and the merchant has a finding
Erasing a customer over SCIM deletes its message log
A merchant's template in its messages document replaces the built-in message, inside the built-in layout
A messages document whose template does not render is refused on load, naming the event type and the error, and the built-in messages send
Each cancellation cause sends one confirmation in its own words: the customer canceled, staff canceled, or collection stopped after failed payments
A scheduled price change sends its notice: the old and new amounts, the date and how to cancel
A refund sends one refund receipt, whether staff refunded it or the provider reported it, however often it is replayed
The host's message renderer takes precedence over the merchant's templates for the messages it renders
A subscription ended by failed payments sends one confirmation, its ending's, and not the final failure's notice
A staff cancel that ends access now sends one confirmation in staff's words
An access end a refund caused sends no confirmation by default; the refund receipt is sent
The customer messages route lists a customer's messages newest first, paged, with their statuses, attempts, recipients and facts, for the bound merchant only
A preview renders a candidate template against sample data without saving it, and refuses an invalid one with its error
A test message goes to the merchant's alert address only, ten an hour: the request cannot name one, and a merchant without one is refused
Only a mail server's refusal of the recipient is final: a refused sender is retried and opens the merchant's finding, which its next send resolves
A message whose last attempt's job ends while the sender holds it settles failed, not sending
A declined checkout sends no message by default, and turned on it sends none from a sandbox PSP: the decline names its PSP
A refund the refresh finds more than a week after the provider made it, reading on from its last pass, records no receipt; one found minutes late sends one
A void sends one receipt worded as a canceled charge: the customer was not charged
A subscription's first payment sends its receipt: the amount paid and the billing period
A staff refund OpenRails completes more than a week after it was asked sends its receipt
A replayed NMI chargeback batch, its reversal already booked, reverses and revokes nothing again: access the merchant restored after the dispute survives it

A pack buys a merchant's unit at its own price-to-units ratio, bonus packs included: one lot per pack records its units, what was paid and in what currency, deposited from units_sold; the balance shows at the unit's scale, and the lots move with a billing archive
The same units bought in another currency credit the same unit balance; each lot records the currency that paid it and nothing converts
A plan's allowance delivers its units each paid cycle as a recurring lot, and a staff gift in a unit is granted from units_granted with nothing paid

An order priced in a merchant's unit is paid from the customer's balance as it is created, with no payment or provider, and grants its product's keys; its key answers a retry with the same order; a balance short of it is refused insufficient_credits and creates nothing
Usage priced in a unit by rate card holds and draws the unit balance, soonest-expiring lot first, and a card naming no currency prices no unit; usage the units cannot cover is never owed
A lapsed pack is never drawn and its unspent units expire in the unit, once; usage captured while a lot lived posts before it lapses, so the lot pays it and only the rest expires

Refunding a pack's payment takes that lot's unspent units first, refuses a refund whose share is spent, books a chargeback's spent share as consumed, and a won dispute returns what the chargeback took, with no cash leg in the unit

Admission holds a unit balance: a request beyond what is left, or one that holds nothing once it is all held, is refused, and a dollar failed-usage limit binds no unit; a capture prices its overrun in full, its posting takes what the lots hold and records the rest forgiven (usage_postings.forgiven, usage_charged charge: forgiven), never owed, and the customer reads its usage in the unit

Reversals of a multi-line order's pack apply in the order they settle: a chargeback settling before an earlier pending refund takes the line's share first, the refund then takes the rest, each share is recorded once, in the general ledger, and a won dispute restores what the chargeback took

A period in a unit whose volume price falls below what posted is credited once its late window closes, taking back what the period forgave, from the shares its posting stored, before crediting what the lots paid beyond its price
A lease sync's usage in a merchant's unit is refused currency_unsupported and moves nothing: usage in a unit arrives through an admission's capture
The first balance in a unit waits for the units lock a settings change takes before it locks any customer, and records the unit's scale; a gift in a counted unit takes no lock

An order priced in a merchant's unit, paid from lots bought in dollars and euros, has one revenue schedule per paid currency, each funded with exactly the lots' money its spends released: an item recognised at once, a 30-day pass ratably over its window

Cash, payments, attempts, purchases and rebills by outcome or kind equal the measures they replace on one merchant's real sales, refund, won dispute, declines and missed renewal, and a removed measure is refused naming its replacement

The health overview is built from what the merchant sells, every profile's overview saves and answers, an empty merchant's tiles answer with no error, the currency switch keeps each currency's money apart, and saved widgets naming a removed measure are dropped
Every money measure splits by currency unless one currency is named, by PSP and by time too, and money beside a measure with no currency is refused rather than summed
A sale and usage at 23:30 in a merchant's accounting timezone, ten hours behind UTC, count on that local day: date ranges and day buckets start at its midnights and the result names the zone

A day chart across a midnight clock change has one row per local day, the changed day starting at its transition with the sale made on it; the catalogue marks measures read from rollups kept per UTC date
A catalog edit and its history entry commit together, and a refused edit rolls both back
A catalog document records one entry for each object it changes, with its revision and application; a replay records nothing and a removed key is recorded
A configuration change through the API is recorded with its actor, and a credential only as changed, never its value
A Vault document written outside OpenRails is recorded once as Vault's when several replicas load it, and an edited file once as the file's however many processes start on it
The configuration history lists one merchant's entries newest first, by object and time, a page at a time, to merchant configuration readers only
A product's revision shows on its reads, advances on a key change and never on a price change, and its entries carry it
A product edit, archive, key change or delete naming a stale expected revision is refused with revision_mismatch naming the current one, records nothing, and the current revision succeeds

A Stripe chargeback records one dispute with its network, reason family, code and due date, books one reversal, ends the subscription and its access, blocks the card and asks staff to review the customer; replays change nothing
A CCBill chargeback is recorded with its reason, card network and reversal, its outcome unreported
Mastercard's ratio divides a month's chargebacks by the previous month's sales, Visa's by the month's own
The VAMP level in force is the evaluated month's: 2.2% in March 2026, 1.5% from April
A staff refund carries its reason, requested_by_customer unless named; a Stripe dashboard refund carries Stripe's; refunds count in no dispute ratio
A won dispute books its recovery and stays won against a late notice that it opened; a lost one stays lost against a late notice from before the decision

Chargebacks that bring a PSP's ratio to its acquirer limit's warning raise one high finding that alerts; at the limit it escalates to critical and alerts again; sales settling afterwards re-evaluate and resolve it; minimums are actual counts
A charged-back card is never charged again: the customer's other engine subscription on it keeps its paid period and waits for another card, while one on their other card renews on it
A chargeback blocks the card its charge was taken from, never the card the subscription moved to since
A dispute update or an early fraud warning on a charge OpenRails does not know is answered with a finding, never retried

An NMI chargeback batch records every entry with its code: a matched entry is its charge's, reversed, linked and its subscription canceled; an unmatched one takes the masked number's network, books nothing and still counts in the monitor
The network rollup is derived and leaves no row in an archive: a restored book rebuilds it from its payments, disputes and fraud reports, equal to the source's, and its program standings with it

An RDR resolution books one refund (dispute_prevention), whichever of it and Stripe's own refund arrives first, and records the refund it absorbed; a stale inquiry notice reopens nothing; a CE 3.0 block books nothing; neither counts in a ratio

The dispute metrics equal the records: disputes by kind, reason, outcome and the disputed charge's kind, the win rate, the chargeback rate by network, the VAMP ratio with Visa's lines and ECM's with Mastercard's, fraud reports by outcome and refunds by reason; a card merchant's overview carries the dispute programs widget, whose read answers

A Stripe inquiry books, cancels and revokes nothing, its closing undoes nothing, its escalation books the chargeback once, and the reconcile pull records it without proposing it; a chargeback an advisory pull found waits for the merchant to be armed, or for a provider's notice of it

An actionable early fraud warning is a fraud report Visa counts once; without waiting for the deployment's destructive switch it refunds the charge in full once (fraud_warning, fraudulent at Stripe), ends what it paid for and blocks the card whatever events repeat it; the merchant's own stop holds it; one an event calls unactionable is not acted on; a charge in dispute is not refunded; a charge with nothing left to refund is still ended; recording reports only refunds nothing; below a full posture the response waits with one alerting finding and runs when the posture is raised
An operation's attempting entry is written before its provider call and outlives the process dying mid-call; recovery only appends
A subscription's history reads its provider operations from the operations history, each entry once with its phase, kind, attempt and attribution
A price key's moves to a new version, an archive and back are configuration history entries with the key's revision, and a price's history reads them
The breaker marks a destructive attempt sent before its provider call, and its phases are written ahead with their actor
A price migration's source archive waits for the catalog lock another writer holds, then is recorded once, as the migration's, with the key's move to nothing
A parked or stale claim never counts as sent: a stale executor marks nothing, and a park of an admitted attempt clears its mark
Each refusal is stored with its outcome, cause and the PSP's and network's advice, approvals with neither, and the attempt list filters by outcome and cause
An NMI catch-all decline is classified by the issuer's code the Query API reports: a never-retry code waits for a new card and never cancels, a retryable one keeps the schedule
A Stripe renewal Radar blocked is the merchant's refusal and waits for a new card; an issuer's fraudulent decline stays the issuer's

Newly mapped codes decline with their cause: NMI 461 is the merchant account's brand, and Stripe's do_not_try_again, new_account_information_available, service_not_allowed, mobile_device_authentication_required, invalid_amount and testmode_decline have their reasons

Mastercard retry-after advice (MAC 24 to 30) delays the next dunning retry; a delay past the case's window keeps the subscription past due, retries at the advised time and recovers, never asking for another card
New card data (MAC 01, confirm_card_data) is update_cardholder_data, and cards that won't recur (MAC 40, 41) wait for a new card

Authorization rate, issuer-discretion decline rate and first-try rebill approval read the stored outcomes and causes: refusals and errors are in neither, missed renewals in neither; the decline mix and Visa categories, and cuts by kind, card brand, BIN, token type and whether the storing transaction's id was sent; the dimensions decline_cause renamed are refused with their new names; the overview shows them as tiles and in Payment health
NMI history months carry each answer's outcome and cause: a catch-all 200 by the issuer's code, 461 as the merchant account's refusal
The system-errors finding counts the rail's own processing errors, not an issuer's failure behind a generic decline
An engine NMI renewal declined with 200 reads the issuer's code after the decline, or from the order read when the answer was lost; a failed read keeps NMI's own code
An issuer that keeps deferring past the next renewal leaves the case past due with no retry until that renewal, then ends it exhausted as issuer_deferred
A retry that runs late without advice, past the next renewal, keeps dunning with the attempts the policy has left
A weekly plan whose first decline is advised past its renewal (MAC 30) stays past due with no retry, and ends at the renewal as issuer_deferred

The decline-cause migration classifies existing attempts and NMI history months from their stored codes, merges months one reason now covers, keeps each attempt's action, drops saved widgets naming a dimension it renamed, and widens saved declined and error filters to exactly what they meant
A new card on a case the old card's advice deferred is not held to that advice: its plain decline keeps dunning, and the case ends as the card failed, not issuer_deferred
A monthly plan bought mid-month posts its cash to its PSP's clearing account, defers it, and recognises at the month boundary and the period end
An annual calendar plan recognises a twelfth a month across a leap February; a non-UTC accounting zone's boundary follows DST
Lifetime access is recognised at once, a time-limited pass ratably over its window, and seats are funded per seat
A Stripe invoice with non-cash credit, NMI and CCBill rebills and a Solana pull in USDC book cash to their PSPs and recognise from payment
A seat increase defers its charge over the rest of the period
An idle recognition pass takes no schedule; a replayed boundary or order posts once
An external payment books to external_receipts; a payment beyond its bill stays unapplied
An immediate cancellation without a refund forfeits the remainder
A usage order's card and remitted payments book their cash and leave it for the receivable
Revoked access ends its schedule; an undone revocation takes the forfeit back
A late payment on an expired order whose product another order holds stays unapplied
A purchase is applied over the access its grant gives; a replay applies an order with no schedule
A prune that hides booked money or a recognising subscription raises a finding its undo resolves
An end before the schedule exists reaches it: a charge after a cancellation is forfeited at payment
ledger-audit warns of revenue lines completed before the books started and of a provider's tax line, skips a merchant's own unit, and fails a line completed since
An order applied again after a payment sorting earlier arrives applies no payment beyond what it brought
An imported purchase is applied over the access its import grants
A $50 pack of 55 credits defers its price from its payment; 11 credits release exactly $10 and the last credit releases the remainder
A lapsed pack's unreleased money is breakage, a revoked pack's is forfeited, and reinstating it reverses the forfeit and lets it be revoked again
A gift's spend grosses usage up against promotional credit; owed is receivable and is repaid at face from a gift and from a bonus pack
A refund of unspent credit returns its deferred money, a chargeback of spent credit is contra-revenue, and a won dispute reverses it
An archive with a reinstated pack and a pack from before the credit books restores, each lot keeping its money
A won dispute repays again only owed still outstanding: the rest returns to the balance with its money, and the payment refunds after
Two partial recoveries of a chargeback, with and without reopened owed, follow the units they restore and end exact
Owed that accrued partly before the credit books is repaid through the receivable first and the rest as revenue, from a gift and a pack
Refunds in pieces strand no deferred money, and a merchant-unit lot refunds its units in the unit and its money in its paid currency
A revocation retried under its idempotency key after a reinstatement replays, and a lapsed lot is not reinstated
A credit lot applied beyond its payment's cash fails ledger-audit, as a bill's lines would
A credit lot whose payment brought no cash defers nothing, raises books.credit.unapplied and commits
Two billing passes started together: one runs its scans and the other exits without a report; the running pass holds a lease row, not a database session
A billing pass whose holder died leaves a lease that lapses on its own; a pass started meanwhile exits, and the next takes what is due

Of concurrent pulls of one merchant one runs and the others skip, another merchant's pull runs beside it, and a provider refresh waits for the running pull; the pull holds a lease row, not a database session
A pull that runs past one lease period keeps its lease and others still skip; a dead holder's lease lapses on its own and the next pull takes it
